metadata.title: AICTE PS 26262 — Supplementary Rules to Add or Verify
metadata.purpose: Supplement the existing AICTE_PS26262_DETAILED_RULES.json with additional system rules and AICTE-specific rule areas that should be implemented or verified for the prototype.
metadata.important_notice: This file is not an official AICTE rulebook. AICTE-specific regulatory rules remain unverified until mapped to the applicable official handbook, amendments, notices, tables, and annexures. Do not enforce unverified regulatory rules as binding decisions.
metadata.merge_instruction: Merge or reference this file alongside AICTE_PS26262_DETAILED_RULES.json. Preserve the original rule IDs and avoid duplicate IDs when integrating.

status_vocabulary.verified: Confirmed against an authoritative source with exact source reference and applicability recorded.
status_vocabulary.implemented: Code exists; this does not establish regulatory correctness.
status_vocabulary.tested: A named test ran and passed in a recorded environment.
status_vocabulary.proposed: Suggested system behavior that needs team approval.
status_vocabulary.unverified: Insufficient evidence to confirm the exact regulatory requirement or implementation.
status_vocabulary.blocked: Requires an authoritative source, product decision, or human approval.
status_vocabulary.advisory_only: May surface information but must not determine approval, rejection, or compliance automatically.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Application eligibility and route selection
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Determine the applicable processing route from verified application attributes and the applicable official route matrix. If a required attribute is missing, contradictory, or unsupported, route the case to manual review rather than guessing.
expected_behavior: record route and route-matrix version
record the input facts supporting route selection
block automatic routing when required facts are unknown
allow authorized review of ambiguous cases
must_not: infer a binding route from an LLM response
apply one generic workflow to all application types
acceptance_tests: known supported case selects the expected configured route
missing required route attribute creates a review-needed result
unsupported application type is not silently routed to approval
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Map each route to the exact applicable AICTE handbook table/clause and any applicable notice.
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.activation: Do not treat as a regulatory rule until the official route matrix is verified.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Structured deficiency records
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Represent each deficiency as a structured record rather than free text alone.
expected_behavior: preserve the original finding
link finding to the relevant rule and evidence version
track institution response and officer resolution separately
retain history after correction or closure
acceptance_tests: finding is traceable to rule and evidence
institution response does not overwrite officer finding
closure requires authorized actor and resolution reason
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Product/system requirement; regulatory severity and response periods require source confirmation.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Revalidation after resubmission
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: When an institution uploads a corrected or replacement document, rerun applicable checks against the new document version and preserve prior results.
expected_behavior: create a new immutable document version
mark impacted findings as requiring revalidation
record which checks were rerun
do not automatically close findings without successful rule evaluation or authorized review
acceptance_tests: replacement document creates a new version
prior OCR/rule results remain auditable
failed OCR or unavailable source leaves the finding unresolved
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: System behavior; align resubmission limits and process with the applicable official workflow.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Decision authority and human oversight
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Only authorized human roles may perform final regulatory decisions. OCR, deterministic checks, and AI may produce evidence or preliminary findings but must not independently approve or reject an application.
expected_behavior: enforce authority on the backend for each transition
record actor, role, action, reason, timestamp, and relevant evidence
separate recommendation from final decision where the workflow requires it
acceptance_tests: AI output cannot trigger final approval/rejection
unauthorized role cannot execute a restricted transition
decision records the authorized human actor
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Confirm the precise decision authority and stage permissions against the applicable official process and approved project scope.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Document status, validity, and version handling
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: A document must not be considered valid merely because a file exists. Track document type, version, processing status, validity dates where applicable, verification outcome, and reviewer status.
expected_behavior: distinguish missing, uploaded, unreadable, processing, flagged, verified, rejected, and expired states as appropriate
tie extraction and findings to a specific version
require review for contradictions or uncertain extraction
keep replaced versions in audit history
acceptance_tests: expired document is flagged when a verified rule requires validity
unreadable document is not marked compliant
replaced document does not erase previous evidence
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Required document types and validity conditions must be configured by application category and official source.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Safe assignment and reassignment
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Assignment must enforce active-user status, role eligibility, jurisdiction/scope, and uniqueness rules. Reassignment must record the actor, reason, old assignee, new assignee, and timestamp.
expected_behavior: handle no eligible officer without silently dropping the case
prevent duplicate active assignments where prohibited
preserve assignment history
apply conflict-of-interest exclusion only when an approved policy and implementation exist
acceptance_tests: ineligible role cannot be assigned
no-eligible-assignee condition is visible
reassignment leaves an audit event and history
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Confirm official assignment policy and conflict-of-interest rules; do not invent them.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Deterministic deadline calculation
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Every deadline policy must define the triggering event, applicable case types, duration, calendar/working-day convention, timezone, holiday calendar if relevant, extensions, pause/resume behavior, escalation policy, and source/version.
expected_behavior: store the policy version used for each calculated deadline
recalculate only under an explicit policy/event rule
preserve previous deadline values and reasons for changes
distinguish official deadlines from internal reminder thresholds
acceptance_tests: same inputs and policy version yield same deadline
deadline changes record reason and actor/system event
internal reminder thresholds are not labelled as official regulatory deadlines
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: All regulatory durations and trigger dates require exact official source confirmation.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Reliable and idempotent notifications
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Notification processing must not duplicate alerts on repeated sweeps and must not corrupt workflow state when delivery fails.
expected_behavior: record event, recipient, channel, attempt count, result, and timestamps
use an idempotency key
retry according to configured policy
expose failed delivery for operations review
acceptance_tests: repeated sweep does not create duplicate active alerts for the same event/key
delivery failure is recorded
workflow transaction remains consistent when notification provider is unavailable
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Channel, retry schedule, and escalation recipients are product decisions unless official requirements specify otherwise.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Concurrent edit and transition protection
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Reject or safely resolve stale updates so simultaneous officers cannot silently overwrite each other's decisions or transition a case from an outdated state.
expected_behavior: check expected state/version on writes
use transactions for workflow state, assignment, and required audit records
return a clear conflict response for stale writes
avoid partial commits
acceptance_tests: two conflicting concurrent transitions cannot both succeed
stale update receives a conflict response
failed transaction does not leave inconsistent state or audit records

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Explicit exception and terminal-state handling
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Withdrawal, reopening, appeal, closure, rejection, failed processing, and other exceptional paths must have explicit permitted transitions, authority, reasons, and audit behavior; do not infer these from ordinary transitions.
expected_behavior: configure each supported exception separately
reject unsupported transitions
record required reason and authority
preserve prior decisions and workflow history
acceptance_tests: unsupported transition is denied
reopening requires configured authorization and reason
withdrawal does not erase application or audit history
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: The existence, authority, and conditions for each regulatory route must be verified.

important_rules_to_add_or_verify.name: Conflict-of-interest controls for committee assignments
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.rule: Before implementing conflict-of-interest declarations, exclusions, or automatic reassignment, confirm the approved policy and the committee/assignment data model.
expected_behavior: keep feature disabled or advisory until approved
if enabled, record declaration, decision, reviewer, exclusion, and reassignment history
acceptance_tests: no automatic exclusion is applied using an unapproved rule
enabled policy is tested for declaration, review, exclusion, and audit
important_rules_to_add_or_verify.source_requirement: Obtain the applicable official or project-approved conflict-of-interest policy.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Application-type and processing-route matrix
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Create a versioned matrix mapping each in-scope application type and relevant institution/programme attributes to the applicable processing stages and decision authority.
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Verify against the applicable APH version, tables, clauses, annexures, notices, and approved project scope. The candidate list is not a claim that every item is in prototype scope.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Stage-specific scrutiny, visit, committee, and appeal paths
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Specify exactly which application categories and outcomes require SCR/re-SCR, EVC, hearing committee, Executive Committee, appeal committee, or other stages. Do not route all cases through all stages by default.
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Confirm exact official terminology, conditions, order, and authority for the applicable academic year.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Submission windows, cut-offs, fees, and tracking
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Where in scope, record official application windows/cut-offs, fee requirements, submission timestamp, receipt/reference number, and any published exceptions. Enforce a cutoff only when the applicable notice and time basis are verified.
expected_behavior: store source and effective period
distinguish draft from successfully submitted applications
preserve submission receipt and timestamp
do not hardcode annual dates without versioning
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Use the applicable official public notice, APH, and fee schedule. Do not assume dates or fee amounts.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Lease duration and extension requirements
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Implement lease-duration and extension checks only after confirming the applicable clause, required remaining duration, relevant programme/course duration, exception conditions, and accepted evidence.
expected_behavior: calculate remaining duration using a documented date convention
flag missing or contradictory dates
show calculation and source clause
route uncertain cases to human review
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Do not use a generic 'lease nearing expiry' threshold as an official compliance rule without the applicable clause.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Appeal eligibility, authority, and deadline
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: For Chapter II applications, an institution/applicant aggrieved by an Executive Committee decision may appeal once to the Council within 7 days of decision upload. The Standing Appellate Committee considers the appeal; AICTE notifies the hearing schedule; the institution presents compliance/supporting documents through two authorized representatives with self-attested photo ID; SAC recommendations go to the Council, whose decision is final and uploaded to the portal.
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source: SRC-APH-APPEAL-2024-27; AICTE Approval Process Handbook 2024-27, Chapter II §§2.23.3, 2.24(a-f), PDF pp. 44-45 (printed pp. 29-30). Verified 2026-10-27 by named reviewer reyyishreyas and independently fetched by Codex.
expected_behavior: accept one appeal by the institution/applicant against an Executive Committee decision within 7 calendar days from decision upload
preserve appeal submission receipt and supporting evidence links
record the SAC schedule, two authorized representatives and their self-attested photo ID evidence
record SAC hearing recommendation and route it to Council
record Council final decision and portal publication
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Verified for Chapter II appeals only. Do not widen to other application chapters, decision-makers or outcomes without their source clauses. The application role permissions are prototype ACL assignments, not evidence of official delegation.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Required documents by application category
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Maintain a versioned checklist of required documents and accepted alternatives by application category, institution type, programme, and applicable academic year.
expected_behavior: distinguish missing from not applicable
allow documented exception only where permitted
record checklist version on the application
do not auto-reject solely because a proposed checklist has not been verified
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Extract from the applicable APH clauses/tables/annexures and notices; cite exact references for each item.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Stage and role decision-authority matrix
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Map each workflow action and decision outcome to the authority specified by the applicable process, separately from generic software roles.
expected_behavior: deny unauthorized decision actions on the backend
separate recommendation from decision where applicable
record acting user and capacity
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Confirm authority and delegation from official sources and approved institutional workflow.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Regulatory deadline and penalty schedule
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Maintain versioned schedules for submission deadlines, appeal periods, security-deposit proof milestones, penalties, and withdrawal or other cutoff consequences only where confirmed applicable.
expected_behavior: store the source clause, trigger, academic year, category, duration, amount/rate if applicable, and effective dates
calculate with deterministic logic
show calculation to reviewer
keep internal reminders separate from official penalties
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: The 15-day security-deposit proof period and penalty/cutoff dates mentioned in project notes are unverified examples until checked against the applicable official source.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Security deposit and post-grant evidence tracking
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: If security-deposit/FDR tracking is included in the prototype, define required evidence, issuer/bank details where applicable, amount, validity, submission trigger, due date, review status, and escalation/penalty handling from verified policy.
expected_behavior: track evidence separately from initial approval checks
record evidence version and reviewer
avoid calculating penalties until the applicable schedule is verified
show upcoming and overdue items with source traceability
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Confirm scope and official requirements before enabling regulatory consequences.

aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.name: Lease and document expiry monitoring
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.rule: Where ongoing monitoring is in scope, track verified expiry dates and generate configurable advance reminders and overdue flags without representing internal reminders as official deadlines.
expected_behavior: store the extracted date, source document version, confidence/review status
require human confirmation for low-confidence or contradictory dates
make reminder thresholds configurable
record each alert and prevent duplicates
aicte_specific_rules_to_verify.source_requirement: Confirm which documents and expiry events must be monitored; reminder lead times are product settings unless prescribed officially.

cross_cutting_requirements.name: Source traceability for every regulatory rule
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: Each regulatory rule must record source ID, exact clause/table/annexure/page, official URL or file reference, effective date range, applicable academic year and category, verification status, and verifier/date.
cross_cutting_requirements.acceptance: No regulatory rule can be enabled if its required source metadata is absent.

cross_cutting_requirements.name: AI output is advisory and evidence-linked
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: OCR/LLM results must be linked to the document version and extraction metadata. Low confidence, malformed output, conflicts, provider failure, or missing source data must remain unresolved and require review.
cross_cutting_requirements.acceptance: No model output can directly change final workflow state or silently mark a case compliant.

cross_cutting_requirements.name: Audit all material changes
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: Audit material changes to route, rule version, evidence version, findings, assignment, deadline, override, transition, and final decision.
cross_cutting_requirements.acceptance: Audit records include actor/system identity, event, timestamp, reason where required, and references to affected entities.

cross_cutting_requirements.name: Test positive, negative, and ambiguous cases
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: For each rule, test passing evidence, failing evidence, missing evidence, contradictory evidence, unauthorized actions, and processing/service failure where relevant.
cross_cutting_requirements.acceptance: Tests state expected status, permitted next action, audit event, and whether human review is required.

implementation_order.name: Regulatory checks and edge cases
deliverables: verified lease and appeal rules where applicable
verified security-deposit/post-grant checks if in scope

open_questions: Which application categories are explicitly in the prototype scope for evaluation?
Which exact APH version and later amendments/notices apply on the target academic year/date?
What are the authoritative stage sequences and decision authorities for each supported route?
What exact documents and accepted alternatives apply to each supported category?
Which deadlines, date triggers, penalty schedules, and exceptions are officially applicable?
Are lease-duration checks, security-deposit/FDR tracking, post-grant monitoring, appeal handling, and reopening required in the evaluated prototype or only future scope?
What assignment and conflict-of-interest policy is approved for the prototype?
Which external OCR/LLM services may receive document content, and what data-handling constraints apply?
